title: Shiv Sharma v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Pankaj Mithal, J.; Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; relegated to appeal under Paragraph 6.8.
headnote: A consumer challenged two electricity demand notices on the footing that a final report had been submitted in the theft FIR. The Court held that assessment of electricity dues and criminal theft are distinct, so non-prosecution does not wipe out assessed dues. The notices were challengeable by appeal under Paragraph 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was dismissed for alternative remedy.
facts: Shiv Sharma filed a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court challenging two electricity demand notices dated 31 October 2017 for Rs.1,03,330 and Rs.26,500. He contended that he was not involved in theft of electric energy, a final report having been submitted in the criminal case that followed the FIR. Counsel appeared for respondents 2 and 3. The Court considered whether the demands could be interfered with in writ jurisdiction.

holding_units.holding: Assessment of electricity dues and theft of electric energy are separate: a final report, or a finding that a theft charge is not worth prosecuting, does not mean the consumer is not liable to pay assessed dues. A demand notice said to be incorrect or illegal may be challenged by appeal under Paragraph 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ was dismissed on that alternative remedy.

not_decided.point: Whether the demand notices dated 31.10.2017 were incorrect or illegal
not_decided.note: Left to the statutory appeal under Paragraph 6.8.
